title: iPhone Pro 2025 Leaks Reveal Near‑Borderless Design, Says 9to5Mac Report
body:
Apple is reportedly gearing up to unveil a dramatically slimmer iPhone Pro line for 2025, with a “near‑borderless” display that pushes the screen almost to the edges of the chassis. Leaks suggest the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will shed a noticeable amount of bezel, adopt a flatter glass‑back design, and feature a new front‑camera housing that blends seamlessly into the display. If confirmed, the redesign would mark the most significant aesthetic overhaul of the flagship series since the 2018 iPhone XS redesign, and could set a new benchmark for premium smartphones.

According to a detailed report from a reputable Chinese technology outlet, Apple is planning to reduce the side bezels to roughly 1.2 mm on each side, a figure that rivals the thinness of the most competitive Android flagships on the market today. The company is also expected to replace the traditional “notch” with a cut‑out that houses the front‑facing cameras and Face ID sensors, allowing the screen to extend further upward. Early renderings show the cut‑out positioned centrally, with a subtle “pill” shape that minimizes visual disruption. Apple’s engineering team is said to be using a new proprietary adhesive and a stronger glass formulation to maintain structural rigidity despite the reduced frame.

Beyond the visual changes, the near‑borderless design could have functional implications. A larger screen‑to‑body ratio means more real‑estate for apps, gaming, and multimedia consumption without increasing the overall device dimensions. Analysts predict that the iPhone 18 Pro will retain a 6.1‑inch display while the Pro Max will edge closer to 6.8 inches, both potentially offering higher peak brightness and improved HDR performance thanks to an upgraded OLED panel. The slimmer bezels also free up internal space, which Apple may use to accommodate a larger battery, a more powerful processor, or an expanded camera module—areas that have seen incremental upgrades in recent generations.

Industry observers note that Apple’s move toward a near‑borderless aesthetic aligns with broader market trends. Samsung, Google, and Xiaomi have already introduced phones with sub‑1‑mm bezels and under‑display camera technology, pressuring Apple to keep pace. However, Apple has historically prioritized reliability and user experience over sheer thinness, often delaying the adoption of under‑display Face ID to avoid compromising security. The reported design suggests Apple is confident it can integrate its biometric system into a slimmer form factor without sacrificing the speed and accuracy that users expect.

The redesign may also signal a shift in Apple’s product strategy. By pushing the envelope on design, the company could rejuvenate consumer excitement ahead of the anticipated rollout of its next‑generation silicon, likely the A18 Bionic chip. A more expansive display combined with a faster processor would reinforce the iPhone’s positioning as the premier platform for mobile gaming, augmented reality, and professional‑grade photography. Moreover, a flatter back panel—potentially made from a new alloy or recycled titanium—could improve durability and reduce the infamous “window‑shopping” dents that have plagued recent models.

Looking ahead, the near‑borderless iPhone Pro line is poised to debut at Apple’s annual September event, where the company traditionally showcases its flagship devices. If the rumors hold true, the iPhone 18 Pro series could set a new design language that will ripple through Apple’s entire product ecosystem, influencing future iPad, Mac, and wearable aesthetics. As competitors scramble to match Apple’s sleek new silhouette, consumers can expect a renewed focus on immersive screens, refined ergonomics, and the seamless integration of hardware and software that has become the hallmark of Apple’s premium offerings.
